descriptionChirho: Qal active participle (יוֹנֵק / הַיֹּנֵק) functioning as a substantive: 'suckling child, nursing infant, baby at the breast.' Designates infants still dependent on mother's milk, often paired with עוֹלֵל ('small child') in contexts of total destruction or divine care (Num 11:12, Deut 32:25, 1 Sam 15:3, 22:19, Isa 11:8, 49:15, Jer 44:7, Lam 2:11, 4:4). English 'nursing child/suckling'; German nursing-Kind; Arabic الرضيع ('suckling'); Hindi दूध-पीता/पीते ('milk-drinking'); Korean 젖먹는-아이 ('breast-feeding child'); Spanish lactante. The participle functions as a noun denoting the agent who sucks.

Hifil participle (מֵינֶקֶת / מֵנִקְתָּהּ / מֵינִיקוֹת) functioning as a substantive: 'nurse, wet-nurse, nursing mother,' the woman who causes an infant to suck. Used for Rebekah's nurse Deborah (Gen 24:59, 35:8), Moses' nurse/mother (Exod 2:7), nursing mothers among Jacob's flocks-metaphor (Gen 32:15/16), and nursing women in contexts of hardship (Isa 49:23, Joel 2:16, Lam 4:3). English 'nurse/her-nurse'; German Amme/saugende; Arabic مرضعة ('wet-nurse'); Hindi धाई/दूध-पिलाने-वाली ('wet-nurse/milk-giving-one'); Korean 유모 ('wet-nurse'); Spanish nodriza/amamantando.

labelChirho: to suck, nurse at the breast (Qal finite verb)
descriptionChirho: Qal finite verb forms (יִינָק, יִינָקוּ, אִינָק) describing the action of sucking or nursing at the breast from the infant's perspective. Used in blessings and curses: Deut 33:19 'they shall suck the abundance of the seas'; Job 3:12 'why the breasts that I should nurse?'; Job 20:16 'he shall suck the poison of asps'; Song 8:1 'that nursed at my mother's breasts'; Isa 60:16, 66:11-12 'you shall suck the milk of nations/be nursed at the breast of kings.' English 'suck/nurse'; Arabic يرضع ('he sucks'); Hindi चूसेंगे/दूध-पीऊँ; Korean 빨리라 ('shall suck'); Spanish mamar ('to suckle').

labelChirho: to suckle, give suck, cause to nurse (Hifil finite verb)
descriptionChirho: Hifil finite verb forms (הֵינִיקָה, וְתֵינִק, וְהֵינִקִהוּ) describing the causative action of giving suck or nursing a child, from the mother's/nurse's perspective. Sarah nursing Isaac (Gen 21:7 'who would have said that Sarah should give children suck?'), Moses' mother nursing him (Exod 2:7-9 'nurse this child for me and I will give thee thy wages'), and other maternal/nurturing contexts. English 'she nursed/nurse him'; German stillen/saeugen; Arabic أرضع ('she nursed/give suck'); Hindi दूध-पिलाएगी/दूध-पिला ('will give milk/give milk'); Korean 젖먹이리라 ('shall give suck'); Spanish amamantar ('to breastfeed').
